rules.message: HOUSE-CONVENTION rule, `apiRoutes.get(...)`-registered codebases only: GET route with no cache-strategy marker on the same line. A codebase that never calls `apiRoutes.get(...)` never satisfies this rule's `require_file` gate and is silently unaffected by it — this is not a general HTTP rule (see `protected-path-no-auth-evidence`/`dev-path-no-guard-hint` below for this pack's framework-neutral rules). PATH SCOPE on top of that gate, disclosed because nothing else announces it: this rule's `file_pattern` is `(?:^|/)api/.*\.(?:ts|tsx|mts|cts|js|jsx|mjs|cjs)$|/routes/.*\.(?:ts|tsx|mts|cts|js|jsx|mjs|cjs)$|/controllers/.*\.(?:ts|tsx|mts|cts|js|jsx|mjs|cjs)$|[Hh]andler\.ts$|[Cc]ontroller\.ts$`, so it only ever scans files under an `api/`, `/routes/` or `/controllers/` path segment, or files whose name ends in `Handler.ts`/`Controller.ts` — and that last pair is `.ts` ONLY, so a `*Handler.tsx` route file is not scanned. Note the anchoring asymmetry: the `api/` arm carries `(?:^|/)`, so a TOP-LEVEL `api/` directory counts, while the `routes/`/`controllers/` arms require a literal leading `/` and a top-level `routes/` directory therefore does not. An `apiRoutes.get(...)` registration anywhere outside those paths is silently not scanned, so zero findings from this rule means "not scanned there", never "every GET route carries a cache marker". Add `// cache: <strategy>` or `// no-cache: <reason>` to the route line. Suppress a vetted case with `// zzop-get-route-no-cache-marker-ok` on that line or the one directly above it.

HTTP route registered under a protected path segment (`/admin/`, `/internal/`) with no witnessed auth evidence — no native middleware/decorator/annotation guard was recognized on this route (Express middleware, NestJS `@UseGuards`/`forRoutes`, Spring method-security annotation, ...), and no adapter injected the `auth-guarded` attribute — either envelope route injects attributes: a whole-tree `analyzeEnvelope` projection's own `attributes` field (Mode A), or an `adapterOverlays` overlay laid on a natively-parsed tree (Mode B). An env check (isProduction/NODE_ENV) gates WHERE code runs, not WHO may call it, so it does not clear this — that axis is `dev-path-no-guard-hint`'s. If a guard exists but isn't recognized, inject the `auth-guarded` attribute by either route above; otherwise add one. Suppress a vetted case with `// zzop-protected-path-no-auth-evidence-ok` (or `# zzop-protected-path-no-auth-evidence-ok` in Python) on the route's registration line or the one directly above it — that needs a READABLE SOURCE LINE, which a whole-tree `analyzeEnvelope` run (Mode A) does not have: it carries no filesystem root, so there this marker AND the disclosure that would name a mistyped marker are both inert. An `adapterOverlays` overlay (Mode B) sits on a natively-parsed tree whose real file is read, so the marker works normally. Under `analyzeEnvelope`, the `auth-guarded` attribute on the envelope’s own `attributes` field is the ONLY way to clear a vetted route: that surface takes a single envelope argument and no config file, so a rule-level `off` is not reachable there.

HTTP route registered under a dev/debug/internal/`__test__`/playground path segment (the test arm is the DUNDER spelling ONLY — a plain `/test/` segment is NOT matched) whose registration line carries no guard-hint keyword (dev/debug/internal/env/guard/isProduction/isLocal/NODE_ENV) as a later, unquoted call argument — a keyword inside the quoted route string, or anywhere before the line's first comma, does not clear this. Risks leaking dev tooling to production. If no guard exists, gate it behind an env check; if one already exists but is not visible as an argument on this line, pass it as a named guard argument here. Suppress a vetted case with `// zzop-dev-path-no-guard-hint-ok` (or `# zzop-dev-path-no-guard-hint-ok` in Python) on the registration line or the one directly above it. THREE channels here read that registration line — the guard-hint carve-out above, this marker, and the disclosure that names a mistyped marker — and a whole-tree `analyzeEnvelope` run (Mode A) carries no filesystem root, so under it all three are inert: a matching route fires even when a guard-hint argument IS present on its line, no marker suppresses it, and a typo is never called out. Nor is there a rule-level `off` there — `analyzeEnvelope` takes a single envelope argument and no config file — so under Mode A this finding cannot be suppressed at all; clearing a vetted route means analyzing the tree natively instead. An `adapterOverlays` overlay (Mode B) sits on a natively-parsed tree whose real file is read, so all three behave normally.
